title: People Ops Hiring, Onboarding, Performance, and Career Development Guide
author: Maya Patel
content:
Purpose
This guide consolidates Redwood Inference’s core People Operations practices for hiring, new-employee onboarding, ongoing performance and feedback cycles, and career development. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, and engineering managers who run interviews and manage direct reports.

Scope
Applies to all full-time and fixed-term employees across Redwood Inference. Contractors and external vendors should follow the contractor onboarding and performance addendum (see related pages).

Key definitions
- Hiring manager: the employee who owns the role and makes the hiring recommendation.
- Interview panel: a cross-functional set of interviewers aligned to the role’s competencies.
- People Ops partner: the operational HR lead who coordinates requisitions, offers, and onboarding logistics.
- Calibration: a process to align rating and promotion decisions across teams.

Hiring process (end-to-end)
1) Requisition and intake
   - Manager opens a requisition in Workday with role spec, level, compensation band, and estimated time-to-fill.
   - People Ops assigns a recruiter and a People Ops partner within 24 business hours.
   - Target: requisition approved within 5 business days.
2) Sourcing and screening
   - External sourcing (recruiter) + internal referral channel.
   - Phone screen with recruiter to validate core skills and compensation alignment.
   - Target: 30% of screened candidates invited to technical interviews.
3) Interview loop and scorecards
   - Standard loop: hiring manager intro (30m), technical assessment (coding or design; 45–60m), role-specific deep-dive (45m), culture and collaboration interview (30m).
   - Each interviewer completes a standardized scorecard within 24 hours. Scorecard fields: competencies, level match, strengths/weaknesses, hire/no-hire recommendation, and notes.
   - Interview panel must include at least one representative from people-ops for senior roles (L5+).
4) Decision and offer approval
   - Hiring manager consolidates feedback and recommends candidate.
   - Compensation approval required from People Ops and Finance for all offers. Director-level or above require sign-off from VP People Ops.
   - Offer letter generated by People Ops; target time from decision to offer = 48 hours.
5) Background check and closing
   - Offers are contingent on background checks (standard employment verification). People Ops coordinates checks.

Hiring metrics and targets
- Time to hire (requisition approved -> offer accepted): target 30 days median.
- Offer acceptance rate: target >= 70%.
- Diversity-of-slate: goal: 40% of interviewed slate from underrepresented pools for senior technical roles.

Interviewer responsibilities and quality
- Complete scorecards within 24 hours.
- Disclose conflicts of interest before interview.
- Provide behaviorally anchored feedback (specific examples).
- Attend interviewer calibration sessions quarterly.

Onboarding (0–90 day program)
Overview: Onboarding is a shared responsibility between People Ops, IT, hiring manager, and the new hire. Our goal is time-to-productivity while ensuring the new hire feels welcomed and supported.

Before day 1 (People Ops + IT)
- Send welcome email with orientation schedule, first-week calendar invites, and required HR paperwork links at least 3 business days prior.
- Provision laptop and required accounts (Slack, Google Workspace, internal services) no later than day 0.
- Provide manager with the 30-60-90 template and first-week checklist.

Day 1–7 (orientation + mission)
- Day 1: People Ops orientation (benefits, payroll, policies), IT check-in, team welcome, and culture session.
- Manager: role clarity meeting, review of goals, intro to immediate projects and stakeholders.
- Assign a peer buddy for 90 days.

30-60-90 plan (example)
- 30 days: Understand codebase, complete security training, deliver a small scoped task.
- 60 days: Take ownership of a feature/area, contribute to sprint planning, start cross-team partnerships.
- 90 days: Lead an initiative, present impact metrics, and set development goals for the next cycle.

Learning and development during onboarding
- Mandatory: Security & compliance, Data Handling, and SRE basics for engineering hires.
- Recommended: Model-serving foundations and Redwood runtime overview (linked in related pages).
- Budget: New hires receive prorated L&D credits (see L&D policy).

Performance and feedback cycles
Cadence and definitions
- Formal performance cycle: semi-annual (mid-year and year-end) reviews for all employees.
- Continuous feedback: managers are expected to provide ongoing feedback and schedule 1:1s weekly/biweekly.
- Calibration: group-level calibration sessions occur after each formal review period.

Manager responsibilities
- Set clear, measurable goals with the direct report within the first 30 days of the cycle. Use SMART criteria.
- Provide timely feedback and document major decision points (promotions, role changes, performance plans).
- Complete performance reviews and calibration prep materials by published deadlines.

Review process (semi-annual)
1) Self-assessment by employee.
2) Manager assessment and collection of peer feedback (3–5 cross-functional collaborators recommended).
3) Calibration meeting to align ratings across teams.
4) Manager delivers results and co-creates the development plan with the employee.
5) For ratings below expectations, manager and People Ops will create a performance improvement plan (PIP) with clear milestones and timeline.

Rating scale and outcomes
- Exceeds expectations, Meets expectations, Needs improvement, Unsatisfactory.
- Promotion recommendations require a documented evidence packet, peer feedback, and calibration approval.

Promotion and leveling guidelines
- Promotion timeline: typical minimum tenure in level is 12 months, but exceptions for exceptional contributions are permitted with calibration approval.
- Promotion packet should include: objective examples of impact, recent project artifacts, manager narrative, and upward/peer feedback.
- Promotion committee meets monthly for L4–L6 promotions and quarterly for executive levels.

Career development and ladders
- Individual contributor ladder and manager ladder are published and include competency expectations across dimensions (technical craft, leadership, cross-team impact, mentorship).
- Learning budget: all employees receive an annual L&D allowance; people-ops maintains the policy and approval flow.
- Mentorship program: opt-in program pairing new hires with senior ICs for 6 months.

Manager guide: practical checklist
- Hiring stage: write a clear role profile, attend intake, commit to interview timeline, complete scorecards.
- First week: 1:1 with new hire daily for first week, introduce to cross-team stakeholders, set 30-60-90 expectations.
- Ongoing: weekly 1:1s, quarterly career conversations, and formal review preparation.
- If performance concerns arise: document issues early, escalate to People Ops for guidance, and start a corrective plan within 30 days of identifying patterns.

Templates and tools (how to use)
- Scorecard template: copy from People Ops folder and paste into interview feedback form.
- 30-60-90 template: manager editable doc; required for all hires.
- Offer letter: People Ops canonical template; do not edit core compensation or legal language without People Ops approval.

Compliance and sensitive cases
- Confidentiality: recruitment records and candidate notes are retained per data-retention policy. Access is limited to People Ops and hiring panel members.
- Accommodations: People Ops will coordinate reasonable workplace accommodations following disclosure.
- Terminations and PIPs: follow the people-ops termination checklist and consult Legal for high-risk cases.

Ownership and escalation
- People Ops is the owner of hiring and onboarding processes.
- Hiring manager owns candidate experience and interview decisions.
- For disputes or policy exceptions, escalate to VP People Ops and Legal as needed.

FAQ (selected)
- "What is the expected time commitment for interviewers?" — Plan for ~2 hours per candidate including prep and scorecard completion.
- "Can external offers be negotiated above band?" — Any above-band offer requires VP People Ops approval and Finance sign-off.
- "What if a new hire needs more ramp time?" — Managers should extend the 90-day plan with People Ops and document support steps.
